      "observed": "REG2.OUT is on +3.3V, while the MCU decoupling capacitors are on a separate +3V3 net. All listed FCC1 and NAVC1 VDD pins are explicitly unconnected rather than tied to either rail.",
      "expected": "The specified 3.3 V regulator rail should power both MCUs. Each MCU VDD pin should be connected to that supply.",

        {"source": "spec", "quote": "3.3 V LDO ... produces 3V3 for \"MCUs and Sensors\""}
      ],
      "impact": "The MCU core supply pins are not powered in this connectivity, so the FCC and NAVC cannot operate as intended; the separate rail naming also leaves the MCU-side decoupling disconnected from the regulator output.",
      "confidence": 1.0
    },

      "category": "open_connection",

      "nets": ["HSE_IN_FCC", "HSE_OUT_FCC", "HSE_IN_NAVC", "HSE_OUT_NAVC", "Net-(C33-Pad1)", "Net-(C53-Pad1)", "Net-(FCC1-PH0)", "VREF+_FCC", "Net-(NAVC1-PH0)", "Net-(NAVC1-PH1)"],
      "observed": "The FCC crystal connects to FCC1.5 (PE6) and FCC1.37 (PE7), not its PH0/PH1 oscillator pins. The NAVC crystal nets do not connect to NAVC1 at all; NAVC1.5 (PH0) and .6 (PH1) instead connect to capacitors to ground.",

        {"source": "spec", "quote": "HSE crystal (both MCUs) | ABM8G-25.000MHZ-4Y-T3"}
      ],
      "impact": "Neither MCU is connected to its intended external high-speed crystal. The FCC crystal is routed to GPIO pins, and the NAVC crystal is isolated from the MCU oscillator pins, preventing intended HSE clock operation.",
      "confidence": 0.99
    },
    {
      "category": "bridged_nets",
      "components": ["FCC1", "UART3_FCC1"],
      "pins": ["FCC1.48", "FCC1.73", "UART3_FCC1.3", "UART3_FCC1.4"],

      "evidence": [
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (name \"UART3_RX_FCC\") ... (node (ref \"FCC1\") (pin \"73\") (pinfunction \"VCAP\"))"},
        {"source": "netlist", "quote": "(net (name \"UART3_TX_FCC\") ... (node (ref \"FCC1\") (pin \"48\") (pinfunction \"VCAP\"))"}
      ],
      "impact": "The UART3 connector exposes and loads the MCU's VCAP regulator outputs instead of UART signals, potentially disrupting the internal core supply and making UART3 unusable.",
      "confidence": 0.99
    }
  ],
  "summary": "Anomalies are present: the MCU VDD pins are unconnected and the regulator output is on a distinct net from the MCU-side 3V3 rail. The crystal connections are also incorrect, and UART3 connector signals are tied to VCAP pins."

anomalies.expected: VCAP pins are internal-regulator outputs and should have the required local capacitors to ground, not be used as UART signals or exposed on a signal connector.
anomalies.impact: The UART3 connector exposes and loads the MCU's VCAP regulator outputs instead of UART signals, potentially disrupting the internal core supply and making UART3 unusable.
